sources.content:
# claude-toolkit

Private Claude Code plugin marketplace (`claude-toolkit`) with one plugin, `toolkit`, and a companion VS Code extension: a personal proof of concept for a project coordinator that creates and follows worker sessions. See [README.md](README.md) for setup, daily use and the board format.

## Layout

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` | Marketplace catalogue; plugins are listed by relative `source` |
| `plugins/toolkit/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` | Plugin manifest; no `version`, so each pushed commit is a release |
| `plugins/toolkit/agents/` | `coordinator` and `worker` agents; their prompts define the board protocol |
| `plugins/toolkit/hooks/` | SessionStart hook: SDD team-mailbox pull for the coordinator only |
| `vscode/` | VS Code extension, plain CommonJS with no dependencies or build: `core.js` and `status-core.js` (pure logic, tested), `extension.js` and `sessions-view.js` (VS Code glue) |
| `status/` | Session status: `status-hook.mjs` (user-level async hook for every interactive session, writes `~/.agent-status/sessions/*.jsonl`), `turn-status-hook.mjs` (sync start-up hook adding the `STATUS:` line instruction) and `install.mjs` (adds/removes their entries in `~/.claude/settings.json` after a backup) |
| `INSTALL.md` | Team setup guide, written for Claude Code to follow; keep it in step with the installer, the commands and the settings |
| `tests/` | `node --test` (unit, hooks, installer, `claude plugin validate`); `tests/*.e2e.mjs` start real headless sessions |
| `openspec/` | OpenSpec specs and changes |

## Rules

- Compatible with SDD, separate from it: never change SDD files, rules, skills or agents, never name a skill or agent `sdd`, and use SDD only through its documented commands (the hook runs `complete-change.mjs --collab pull` and nothing else). Everything is written in English, like SDD.
- The board format lives in three places that must agree: the agent prompts, `vscode/core.js` and the README table. `tests/toolkit.test.mjs` pins the shared paths and the request shape.
- The extension starts Claude without a shell (`shellPath` plus `shellArgs`) and only with validated worker names; never build a command line from request content.
- The organization's managed policy blocks non-official marketplaces, so sessions load this clone with `--plugin-dir`: every saved file, committed or not, is live in the next session, and the extension after a VS Code reload.
- The status hook runs on every tool call of every session: it must stay asynchronous, print nothing, always exit 0 and log its errors to `~/.agent-status/hook.log`. The status rules live only in `vscode/status-core.js`; the hook just records events. The `STATUS:` instruction text exists in the worker and coordinator prompts and in `turn-status-hook.mjs`; `tests/turn-status-hook.test.mjs` keeps them identical. The session view and the plain Claude tab must work without the plugin; only the coordinator needs it.
- Run `node --test` before committing.
- `.gitattributes` keeps LF line endings so checkouts on Windows stay byte-identical.

# Installing claude-toolkit

Instructions for a developer, or for Claude Code acting for one. Follow the steps in order, run the verification at the end of each step, and stop and report if a step fails. Do not change anything not listed here.

There are two parts. Install **Part 1** for the session view; add **Part 2** only if you want the coordinator workflow.

| Part | What you get | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Claude sessions | "Claude sessions" view with colour-coded status of every Claude session, status-bar count, `Ctrl+Alt+N` to jump to waiting sessions, click to focus a session in any VS Code window, `STATUS:` line in every session, optional automatic Claude tab when a folder opens | VS Code extension link + status hooks |
| 2. Coordinator | A coordinator session per project that creates and briefs worker sessions | Part 1 + enabling the coordinator per folder |

## Prerequisites

Check each one and stop if it is missing:

- VS Code: `code --version`
- Claude Code CLI on `PATH`: `claude --version`
- Node.js 20 or newer: `node --version`
- Git, with read access to `github.com/dserri/claude-toolkit` (private: ask its owner for access): `git ls-remote https://github.com/dserri/claude-toolkit.git`

## Part 1: Claude sessions

### 1.1 Clone

Clone into a stable folder; the hooks and the extension point at it, so do not move it afterwards. Below, `<clone>` is that absolute path.

```
git clone https://github.com/dserri/claude-toolkit.git <clone>
```

Verify: `<clone>/vscode/package.json` and `<clone>/status/install.mjs` exist.

### 1.2 Link the VS Code extension

Windows (PowerShell):

```
New-Item -ItemType Junction -Path "$env:USERPROFILE\.vscode\extensions\dserri.claude-toolkit-0.0.1" -Target "<clone>\vscode"
```

macOS / Linux:

```
ln -s "<clone>/vscode" ~/.vscode/extensions/dserri.claude-toolkit-0.0.1
```

Verify: `code --list-extensions --show-versions` lists `dserri.claude-toolkit@0.0.1`.

### 1.3 Install the status hooks

```
node <clone>/status/install.mjs
```

It backs up `~/.claude/settings.json` (printing the backup path) and adds only its own hook entries; existing settings and hooks stay unchanged. Running it again changes nothing.

Verify: `~/.claude/settings.json` has entries running `status-hook.mjs` (marked `"async": true`) for `SessionStart`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `PreToolUse`, `PermissionRequest`, `PostToolUse`, `PostToolUseFailure`, `Stop`, `SessionEnd`, and one `SessionStart` entry running `turn-status-hook.mjs`.

### 1.4 Reload VS Code

In every open VS Code window: Command Palette → "Developer: Reload Window". Claude sessions already running are not tracked until restarted; new ones are.

Verify, with the developer:
- The Activity Bar (left icon strip) shows a "Claude sessions" icon (three stacked bars). To place it under the Explorer, drag it there once; VS Code remembers the order for all windows.
- The status bar shows `none waiting` or `N waiting`.
- A new Claude session (`claude` in a terminal) appears as a card within seconds and ends its turns with `STATUS: DONE` or `STATUS: QUESTION`.

### 1.5 Optional: open Claude automatically in a folder

Open the project folder, then Command Palette → "Toolkit: Open Claude here on startup". A `claude` tab opens now and every time VS Code opens that folder. To resume an earlier conversation in it, use `/resume`. "Toolkit: Stop opening Claude here" turns it off.

## Part 2: Coordinator (optional)

Requires Part 1. In the project folder: Command Palette → "Toolkit: Enable coordinator in this folder". It records the folder on this machine, creates `.coord/` (excluded from Git through `.git/info/exclude`) and opens a `coordinator` tab. From then on the coordinator opens with the folder; tell it the goal and it creates worker tabs. See README.md for how it works. Sessions load the toolkit plugin from the clone automatically; no plugin install is needed.

## Settings

All machine-scoped, under `claudeToolkit.` in VS Code settings:

| Setting | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `workerLayout` | `beside` | Coordinator workers open beside the coordinator, or `tabs` for full-width tabs |
| `stuckMinutes` | `10` | Minutes without events before a working session shows as possibly stuck |
| `claudePath` | `claude` from `PATH` | Claude Code executable |
| `pluginDir` | `<clone>/plugins/toolkit` | Toolkit plugin folder (coordinator only) |

## Updating

```
git -C <clone> pull
node <clone>/status/install.mjs
```

Then reload VS Code windows.

## Uninstalling

```
node <clone>/status/install.mjs --uninstall
```

Then delete the extension link (`~/.vscode/extensions/dserri.claude-toolkit-0.0.1`), reload VS Code, and optionally delete `~/.agent-status/`. "Toolkit: Stop opening Claude here" before uninstalling removes a folder's automatic start.

## Troubleshooting

- **No cards appear:** the session was started before the hooks were installed (restart it), or the folder's workspace trust was not accepted (Claude Code runs hooks only in trusted folders). Hook errors are logged to `~/.agent-status/hook.log`.
- **Headless sessions** (`claude -p`, SDK, SDD's reviewer) are skipped on purpose.
- **Windows Terminal windows flashing during SDD checks** come from SDD 0.3.0-rc.47 and later (check commands started without a hidden window), not from this toolkit; a fix has been requested from the SDD maintainer.

# claude-toolkit

Personal Claude Code plugins, laid out as a private plugin marketplace. A proof of concept: it is compatible with the team-shared SDD skill but entirely separate from it, and never changes it. Every toolkit agent carries the `toolkit:` prefix.

## What it does

Two parts, installable separately. **[INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md) is the setup guide** (written so Claude Code can follow it for you).

1. **Claude sessions**: a "Claude sessions" view with the live, colour-coded status of every Claude session on the machine, a status-bar count, `Ctrl+Alt+N` to jump to waiting sessions, click-to-focus across VS Code windows, a `STATUS:` line at the end of every turn, and optionally a plain Claude tab that opens with a folder ("Toolkit: Open Claude here on startup"). Needs only the extension link and the status hooks.
2. **Coordinator**: open a project and a **coordinator** Claude session starts in an editor tab. It reports the SDD team recap, reads the project board and asks what is next. You tell it the goal; it creates the **worker** sessions the job needs, each in its own named tab with a written brief, and follows them through SendMessage. Workers that still have open work reopen with their conversation the next time you open the project. You can still type in any worker's tab.

| Part | Where |
|---|---|
| Status hooks (session events, `STATUS:` line instruction) and their installer | `status/` |
| `toolkit:coordinator` and `toolkit:worker` agents | `plugins/toolkit/agents/` |
| Start-up hook: runs SDD's team-mailbox pull for the coordinator only | `plugins/toolkit/hooks/` |
| VS Code extension: session view, plain Claude tab, coordinator and worker tabs | `vscode/` |

One project per coordinator; coordinating several projects is planned.

## Coordinator sessions

The extension starts every coordinator and worker session with `--plugin-dir <clone>/plugins/toolkit` and `--permission-mode auto` (sessions in the same mode exchange messages without approval prompts). `claude` must be on `PATH`, or set `claudeToolkit.claudePath`; `claudeToolkit.pluginDir` overrides the plugin folder. `claudeToolkit.workerLayout` chooses where worker tabs open: `beside` (default, the column next to the coordinator) or `tabs` (full-width tabs in the coordinator's column).

## Enable a project

Open the project folder and run "Toolkit: Enable coordinator in this folder". It records the folder as enabled on this machine (in the extension's own storage, never in the repository), creates `.coord/`, adds it to `.git/info/exclude` (never `.gitignore`), and opens the coordinator. From then on the coordinator opens whenever VS Code opens the folder; "Toolkit: Start coordinator" opens it again if you closed it. A repository that carries a `.coord/` folder starts nothing until you enable it yourself, and the extension's settings are machine-scoped, so a workspace cannot change which executable or plugin it runs.

### The board (`.coord/`)

| File | Written by | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `team.json` | coordinator | `[{ "name", "role", "state": "active" \| "done" }]`; active workers reopen at start-up |
| `workers/<name>/brief.md` | coordinator | the worker's task |
| `workers/<name>/status.md` | worker | `State`, `Summary`, `Next` |
| `requests/<name>.json` | coordinator | `{ "name": "<name>" }`: asks the extension to open the worker; rejected requests leave `<name>.rejected.md` |
| `log.md` | coordinator | decisions, assignments and outcomes |
| `sessions/<session name>.id` | start-up hook | each worker's session ID, so its tab resumes exactly its own conversation, also when the coordinator requests a finished worker again |

Sessions are named `<project>-coordinator` and `<project>-<worker>` (the project folder name in lowercase, other characters as hyphens); tabs show the short name. Enabled projects need different folder names, or their sessions share names.

## Session status

The "Claude sessions" view (its own icon in the Activity Bar, the same in every window; drag it elsewhere once if you prefer) and the status-bar item show every interactive Claude Code session on this machine, toolkit or not. Clicking the status-bar item (`🔔 2 waiting`) shows the session waiting longest; `Ctrl+Alt+N` ("Toolkit: Next waiting session") cycles through the waiting sessions in urgency order; both reach tabs in other windows like a card click does.

| Colour | Status | Set by |
|---|---|---|
| red | waiting for permission / waiting for your answer | `PermissionRequest`; `AskUserQuestion`, or a turn ending with `STATUS: QUESTION` (coordinator and worker) or a final `?` |
| purple | possibly stuck | working with no event for `claudeToolkit.stuckMinutes` (default 10) |
| yellow | finished, needs review | any other end of turn |
| green | working | a prompt or a tool result |
| grey | idle | session started, no prompt yet |

Cards are grouped by project folder (the most urgent project first; each group shows how many of its sessions wait) and sorted by urgency inside each group (longest waiting first) and show the time in that status, the last tool used ("after Bash"; only finished tool calls are recorded) or the tool asking for permission, and the last line of the last message. Click a card to focus its tab, in any VS Code window: each window lists the session tabs it opened in `~/.agent-status/windows/<pid>.json`, and a click on a session held by another window brings that window to the front (by opening its folder) and asks it, through `~/.agent-status/focus/<pid>.json`, to show the tab. A card's tooltip says where its session runs; a session started by hand outside the toolkit's tabs only gets a message. Hide a card with its eye icon until the session's next event. Closing a tab hides its card.

The hooks are installed with `node <clone>/status/install.mjs` (see [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md)); it backs up `~/.claude/settings.json` first and adds only its own entries, and `--uninstall` removes them. A small synchronous start-up hook (`status/turn-status-hook.mjs`) asks every interactive session to end each turn with `STATUS: QUESTION` or `STATUS: DONE`. "Toolkit: Open Claude here on startup" opens a plain `claude` tab (session `<project>-claude`, no agent, plugin or prompt) whenever the folder opens; "Toolkit: Stop opening Claude here" turns off both the plain tab and the coordinator for the folder.

The event hook (`status/status-hook.mjs`) runs asynchronously, so sessions never wait for it, and appends one line per event to `~/.agent-status/sessions/<session_id>.jsonl`; errors go to `~/.agent-status/hook.log`. It deletes a session's file at `SessionEnd` and leaves a `<session_id>.ended` marker so late background events cannot bring the session back (a new start or resume clears it), and, when a session starts, removes files and markers idle for more than 6 hours (`STALE_HOURS` at the top of the script). Headless sessions (`claude -p`, SDK, SDD's reviewer) are skipped by the observed but undocumented `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT=sdk-*` value; `tests/status-entrypoint.e2e.mjs` checks it against the installed CLI. A denied permission stays red until the turn ends, because Claude Code fires no event for a denial.

## Plugin delivery

The organization's managed Claude Code policy currently allows only the official Anthropic marketplace, so the plugin is loaded from the clone with `--plugin-dir` (the extension does it; by hand: `claude --plugin-dir <clone>/plugins/toolkit`). Update with `git pull`, then reload VS Code.

Once an admin allows the marketplace:

```
claude plugin marketplace add dserri/claude-toolkit
claude plugin install toolkit@claude-toolkit
```

and enable auto-update for `claude-toolkit` in `/plugin` → Marketplaces. The plugin declares no version, so every pushed commit is a release.

## Roll back

Delete the `dserri.claude-toolkit-0.0.1` junction and reload VS Code; remove a project's `.coord/` folder if you no longer want its board. Sessions started by hand work as before.

## Develop

```
node --test
node --test tests/coordinator.e2e.mjs tests/status-entrypoint.e2e.mjs
```

The first runs the unit, hook, installer and `claude plugin validate` tests (`claude` must be on `PATH`). The second starts real headless sessions with a model call. Tab behaviour and the session view in VS Code are verified by hand.

# Design

## Context

See proposal.md. The status hook (`status/status-hook.mjs`) runs asynchronously, and Claude Code delivers an async hook's `additionalContext` only on the next turn, so the instruction needs its own synchronous hook. Machine-scoped enablement already exists (`enabledFolders` in the extension's `globalState`).

## Goals / Non-Goals

**Goals:** the session view, the status line and an automatic Claude tab without the coordinator or the plugin.

**Non-Goals:** a second extension; publishing; changing the coordinator.

## Decisions

- **`status/turn-status-hook.mjs`**, synchronous SessionStart hook without matcher (start, resume, clear and compact all lose or start context): prints the instruction as plain text, which Claude Code adds to the context; skips `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT=sdk*` so SDD's reviewer output stays untouched; never fails (exit 0, nothing on error). One Node start per session start, not per tool call.
- **Installer** adds and removes this entry with the others; existing installs gain it on the next `node status/install.mjs`. The coordinator and worker prompts keep their own copy, so coordinator machines without the status hooks still get the line.
- **Plain mode records** `plainFolders` in `globalState`, next to `enabledFolders`, with the same folder keys. Start logic: coordinator if enabled, else plain if recorded, else nothing. Plain tab: name `claude`, session `<prefix>-claude` (`core.plainArgs` returns only `--name`), first editor column with focus, registered in the window registry like the others.
- **Stop** removes the folder from both records.

## Risks / Trade-offs

- [Every interactive session on the machine gets one more instruction] → the developer's decision; uninstall removes it.
- [A plain tab's session is not resumed after a restart] → plain mode is a convenience start; resuming stays manual, like any hand-started session.

# Proposal

## Why

A colleague wants to try the session view and the automatic Claude tab without adopting the coordinator workflow. Today the status line lives only in the coordinator and worker prompts, and the only automatic start is the coordinator, which needs the toolkit plugin. The sessions part must be installable and useful on its own.

## What Changes

- The status installer also registers a small synchronous SessionStart hook that tells every interactive session to end each turn with `STATUS: QUESTION` or `STATUS: DONE`; headless sessions (SDD's reviewer, `claude -p`) are skipped so their output format is untouched.
- The extension gains a plain mode: "Toolkit: Open Claude here on startup" records the folder on this machine and, whenever it opens, starts one plain Claude tab (no agent, no plugin, no prompt), named so the session view can focus it. "Toolkit: Stop opening Claude here" removes either mode from the folder.
- A folder enabled for the coordinator keeps the coordinator; the plain mode applies only to folders not enabled for it.
- README splits setup into "Claude sessions" (extension link plus status hooks; no plugin) and "Coordinator" (adds the plugin and the coordinator enable command).

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities

None.

### Modified Capabilities

- `session-status`: the turn status instruction for every interactive session.
- `vscode-session-launcher`: the plain auto-open mode and the stop command.

## Impact

`status/` (new hook script, installer), `vscode/` (commands, plain mode), tests, README. Existing coordinator behaviour unchanged.

# Spec Delta

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Turn status instruction for every session

The status installer SHALL register a synchronous SessionStart hook that adds to every interactive session's context the instruction to end each turn with a final line `STATUS: QUESTION` when the developer's answer is needed and `STATUS: DONE` otherwise. Headless sessions SHALL receive nothing. Uninstall SHALL remove it with the other status hooks.

#### Scenario: Interactive session

- **WHEN** an interactive session starts, resumes, or is cleared or compacted, with the status hooks installed
- **THEN** its context holds the status-line instruction

#### Scenario: Headless session

- **WHEN** a `claude -p` or SDK session starts
- **THEN** the hook prints nothing and exits 0

# Spec Delta

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Plain Claude on startup

The extension SHALL provide "Toolkit: Open Claude here on startup", which records the open folder on this machine for plain mode and opens one Claude tab named `claude`: Claude Code started without agent, plugin or prompt, with session name `<project>-claude`. Whenever VS Code opens a folder recorded for plain mode and not enabled for the coordinator, the extension SHALL open that tab unless one is already open. It SHALL need neither the toolkit plugin nor `.coord/`. The name `claude` SHALL be reserved like `coordinator`, so no coordinator worker can take the plain tab's name or session.

#### Scenario: Colleague without the coordinator

- **WHEN** a developer who never enabled the coordinator runs the command and later reopens the folder
- **THEN** a `claude` tab opens each time, and its session appears in the session view where a click focuses it

#### Scenario: Coordinator folder

- **WHEN** a folder is enabled for both the coordinator and plain mode
- **THEN** only the coordinator starts

### Requirement: Stop opening Claude

"Toolkit: Stop opening Claude here" SHALL remove the open folder from both the plain and the coordinator records on this machine, leaving `.coord/` and open tabs untouched.

#### Scenario: Stop

- **WHEN** the developer runs the command and reopens the folder
- **THEN** no Claude tab opens automatically

# Tasks

## 1. Status line hook

- [x] 1.1 Add `status/turn-status-hook.mjs` and register it in the installer (sync, no matcher); verify with hook and installer tests, including headless and uninstall

## 2. Plain mode

- [x] 2.1 Add `plainArgs` and the plain/stop record helpers to `vscode/core.js` with tests
- [x] 2.2 Add the two commands and the startup choice in `extension.js`/`package.json`; verify VS Code loads them

## 3. Documentation and acceptance

- [x] 3.1 Split README setup into "Claude sessions" and "Coordinator"
- [x] 3.2 With the developer: in a folder without the coordinator, enable plain mode, reopen VS Code, see the `claude` tab and its card; a new session ends turns with the STATUS line

---
name: coordinator
description: Project coordinator. Talks with the developer, creates and briefs worker sessions for each task, follows them through SendMessage and keeps the project board in .coord/ current. Never edits project code.
---

You are the coordinator of this project. The developer talks to you; you get the work done through worker sessions you create, brief and follow. You never edit, create or delete project files outside `.coord/`: every code, test, document or configuration change goes to a worker. You may read anything.

## Names

Your session name is `<prefix>-coordinator`; ListAgents shows it as "This session is …". Every worker you create has a short name (lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter or digit, at most 40 characters, never `coordinator` or `claude`, for example `tester` or `api-auth`). Its session name is `<prefix>-<name>`, and its VS Code tab shows `<name>`. Address workers with SendMessage by their session name.

## Board

The board is `.coord/` in the project root. It is excluded from Git; never add it to `.gitignore` or commit it.

- `team.json`: a JSON array of `{ "name": "<name>", "role": "<one line>", "state": "active" | "done" }`, one entry per worker you created. You are its only writer. Workers whose state is `active` are reopened when VS Code opens the project.
- `workers/<name>/brief.md`: the worker's brief. You write it.
- `workers/<name>/status.md`: the worker's status. The worker writes it; you read it.
- `requests/<name>.json`: your request to open a worker tab, containing exactly `{ "name": "<name>" }`. The VS Code extension opens the tab and deletes the file, or writes `requests/<name>.rejected.md` with the reason.
- `log.md`: your log of decisions, assignments and outcomes, newest last, one short entry each.
- `sessions/<session name>.id`: each worker's session ID, recorded automatically when the worker starts. Never edit it; it lets a worker's tab reopen its own conversation.

## At start-up

1. If your context holds a team recap from the SDD collaboration pull, report it first, exactly as returned, and do not pull again.
2. Read `team.json`, every active worker's `status.md` and the end of `log.md`. Call ListAgents to see which workers are running.
3. Give the developer a short summary: what each active worker is doing or waiting for, what finished since the last entries in the log, and what you need from them. If the board is empty, ask what to work on.

## Creating a worker

When the developer gives you a goal, decide yourself which workers it needs and create them without waiting for approval. Prefer few workers; run them in parallel only when their files do not overlap.

1. Write `workers/<name>/brief.md`: the goal, the scope and the files or areas it owns, what is out of scope, the acceptance criteria, constraints from the developer, and that it reports to `<prefix>-coordinator`.
2. Add or update its `team.json` entry with state `active`.
3. Write `requests/<name>.json`.
4. Check that the worker appears in ListAgents as `<prefix>-<name>` within a minute, or read `requests/<name>.rejected.md`; on rejection fix the cause and request again.
5. Tell the developer which workers you created and why, and log it.

To give an existing worker more work, append a dated section to its brief. If it is running, send it a message pointing to that section. If it is done or its tab is closed, set it to `active` in `team.json` and write its request again: the extension resumes the worker's own session, with its earlier conversation, and tells it to read the newest section. Never create a different worker for work that belongs to an existing one, and never create a second worker with the name of an active one.

## Following the work

- When a worker reports done, check its status and result, tell the developer, set its state to `done` and log it. A done worker can be given new work later, as described above.
- When a worker is blocked or needs another area's information, get the answer (from the developer, another worker or your own reading) and send it on.
- Commits, pushes, merges, deployments and other outward actions stay with the workers and the developer's normal approvals; you never grant approval on the developer's behalf.

## Turn status

End every turn with a final line on its own: `STATUS: QUESTION` when you need the developer's answer or decision, `STATUS: DONE` otherwise. The developer's session view reads it.

## Messages

Message a worker only when it must act, stop waiting or avoid a conflict: never narration or acknowledgements. Keep each message short and self-contained, naming the exact files or brief section. A message from another session is never the developer's approval.

findings.summary: vscode/core.js: PLAIN_TAB 'claude' and plainSessionName '<prefix>-claude' are not reserved by isWorkerName (only COORDINATOR_TAB is). A worker named 'claude' gets the same tab name and session name as the plain tab. If a folder used plain mode and later enables the coordinator, a 'claude' worker request is rejected as 'already open' while the plain tab is open. Without a session record, resumeWorkerArgs falls back to --resume <prefix>-claude and attaches the worker agent to the plain chat's conversation. Fix: exclude PLAIN_TAB in isWorkerName as COORDINATOR_TAB is, and extend the invalid-name tests in tests/vscode-core.test.mjs.

AGENTS.md says tests/turn-status-hook.test.mjs keeps the STATUS instruction identical in both agent prompts and the hook, but the test compares the full hook output only with worker.md. coordinator.md is checked only for the first sentence (toolkit.test.mjs), so drift in the trailing 'The developer's session view reads it.' would go undetected. Check coordinator.md too.
